evals.prompt: Review the information architecture of this mobile settings area. Current global tabs: Home, Projects, More. More contains Notifications, Billing, Team members, Export data, and Log out. The Settings page groups rows in backend API order and every row has a right chevron. Provide an IA review only; do not redesign visual styling.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based IA findings separating navigation placement, grouping/order, and labels, with visual issues handed off.
expectations: Separates frequent/global, contextual, and rare/account-level actions when recommending placement.
Flags Log out in the catch-all More menu and places it in account/profile settings.
Flags backend/API ordering and recommends a user-priority or mental-model grouping.
Keeps the review within IA scope and hands visual styling or contrast concerns to a visual design review.

evals.prompt: Audit these labels across an app: top nav has 'Updates'; the page title is 'Notifications'; a CTA says 'View activity'; empty state says 'No messages yet'; settings uses 'Alert preferences'. The destination contains system alerts and project change history. Review labels and information scent only.
evals.expected_output: A label inventory that identifies inconsistent concepts, proposes a coherent vocabulary, and explains destination predictability.
expectations: Inventories or explicitly compares all five labels rather than reviewing one in isolation.
Identifies that alerts/notifications and activity/history are distinct concepts that should not be collapsed without evidence.
Recommends labels based on destination content and user expectation, not merely brevity.
Does not drift into color, spacing, or implementation advice.

evals.prompt: Nothing is built yet. We're designing Relayd: an agent that watches a shared support inbox, drafts replies, and asks a human to approve each one before sending. Ops leads configure which mailboxes it watches and what it may send without approval. Support agents review drafts. How should this be structured?
evals.expected_output: A Mode 3 structure proposal whose conditional agentic step is run — actors, responsibility, persistent objects, handoffs, re-entry and provenance settled before the navigation model — with intent-based grouping preserved.
expectations: Routes to Mode 3 (structure design) because nothing is built, rather than auditing a sketch.
Runs the conditional agentic step and names the actors separately from the people — asking user, agent, human reviewer, operator, and the customers who receive the sent replies.
Assigns recovery ownership explicitly, not only initiation and approval.
Gives each persistent object it needs (task, plan, run, result, source, permission, approval, history) a home, or states deliberately that it needs none.
Designs re-entry for running, completed, failed and paused work as distinct retrieval needs rather than one 'Activity' list.
Groups destinations by user intent and does not turn the object checklist into the navigation — a top-level 'Runs' tab appears only with a stated reason.
Says where the record of what the agent did and what it rested on survives after the session.
Stays in IA scope and hands visual and implementation concerns to the sibling skills.

evals.prompt: Create an IA blueprint for a dense B2B returns operations app. Agents work a queue all day, open a return, inspect evidence, approve or reject it, and then move to the next item. Leads use saved views and bulk reassignment. Filters and selected tabs currently disappear on refresh. Give us a build-time structure, not visual styling.
evals.expected_output: A dense-SaaS blueprint grounded in repeated operational work, durable retrieval state, and queue-to-detail re-entry rather than a generic dashboard template.
expectations: Uses Mode 3 and the dense operational blueprint as a form, while tracing every destination back to the supplied tasks.
Distinguishes durable destinations from temporary filters and saved views.
Assigns URL or persistent ownership to filters, sort, selected tabs and saved views so refresh and deep links behave predictably.
Designs queue to detail to next-item flow without forcing agents back through a dashboard.
Keeps lead-only bulk administration distinct from the agent's primary work surface.
Names responsive structural behaviour as still owed to ui-design-principles rather than pretending the IA blueprint settled it.

evals.prompt: Create the navigation and labeling blueprint for a bilingual Japanese/English documentation site. It has getting-started guides, task guides, API reference, troubleshooting, versioned pages, search, and long local tables of contents. Some translated navigation labels are roughly twice the English length.
evals.expected_output: A content-site blueprint with complementary retrieval routes, canonical homes, version context, and localization-aware label validation.
expectations: Organises content by durable audience questions or topics rather than publishing-team ownership.
Separates hierarchy (breadcrumbs), association (related links), local navigation, browse and search as different retrieval mechanisms.
Assigns every page a canonical home and makes version/applicability visible where it changes interpretation.
Tests labels against both Japanese and English content rather than shortening one language to fit an assumed layout.
Keeps visual truncation and responsive implementation as handoffs while resolving the information structure and canonical vocabulary here.
